productContext:
Product: Fieldnote (https://fieldnote.example)
One-liner: A note-taking app for field researchers.
Summary: Fieldnote is an offline-first notebook for researchers who collect observations away from a desk: ecologists, archaeologists, anthropologists and UX researchers on site visits. Notes carry GPS, time, photos and audio automatically, follow reusable observation templates, and sync to a shared project when the connection comes back.
Audience: Graduate students, field technicians and small research teams who take structured notes outdoors or on site, often without signal, and later need to analyze or share them.
Problem: Field notes end up split between a paper notebook, a phone's camera roll and a spreadsheet typed up at night. Transcribing takes hours, locations and times get lost, and teammates can't see each other's observations until someone merges them.
Positioning: For field researchers who juggle paper notebooks, photos and spreadsheets, Fieldnote is an offline-first field notebook that captures structured observations with location and media, and syncs them to the team. Unlike general note apps, it's designed for days without signal and data that needs to be analyzed later.
Value: Works fully offline; syncs when you're back in range; Every note is stamped with location, time and weather; Observation templates (transects, interviews, site surveys) keep data consistent across a team; Photos, audio and sketches live next to the note they belong to; Export to CSV, GeoJSON or Markdown for analysis
Differentiators: Built for no-signal sites, not adapted from an office note app; Structured templates and free text in the same note; Shared projects with per-site permissions for labs and field schools
Personas:
- Ecology grad student: Runs transects and plot surveys for a thesis, often alone and far from signal. Pains: Retyping paper notes every evening; Photos and GPS points that don't match up with notes; Losing a notebook to rain
- Field school instructor: Teaches archaeology or ecology field methods to 10–30 students each summer. Pains: Every student records differently; Collecting and grading notebooks is slow; No view of what was recorded where
- UX researcher on site visits: Does contextual inquiry at customer sites and needs quick, tagged notes with photos. Pains: Notes scattered across a laptop, phone and sticky notes; Hard to share raw observations with the team quickly
Alternatives people use: TerraJot, Quadrat, Logbook Pro
Owner's notes: We're two people. Focus on ecology and social-science grad students first; university lab licenses come later. Don't promise a desktop app yet.
